plan: [ This is a sealed-bid second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values. Truthful bidding is a weakly dominant strategy: bidding my value maximizes expected profit because the bid only determines whether I win, not the price I pay (which equals the second-highest bid). There is no past history to exploit and only one round. I will bid exactly my value, $36, to win whenever competitors’ top bid is below 36 and avoid winning at a price above my value. ]

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: your bid only affects whether you win, not the price you pay (the second-highest bid sets the price). Shading risks losing when winning would be profitable; overbidding risks negative profit if you accidentally win above value. With independent, uniformly drawn values each round, truthful bidding maximizes expected long-run profit. My value is $8, so bid 8.

[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. This ensures you win exactly when the second-highest bid is below your value and pay that second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit. With value 44 and no prior rounds to learn from, shading reduces winning chances without lowering payment when winning. Therefore, bid 44 to capture all profitable wins while avoiding overpaying. ]
